**Ivy League schools – the four with the smallest endowments (2023‑24) and the number of Nobel laureates they have produced (faculty + alumni, as reported by each school’s Wikipedia “Nobel laureates” count)**  

| Rank (by endowment) | University | Endowment (FY 2023‑24) | Approx. Nobel laureates affiliated* |
|---------------------|------------|------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| 1 (smallest) | **Dartmouth College** | **≈ $4.0 billion** | **≈ 22** |
| 2 | **Brown University** | **≈ $5.4 billion** | **≈ 33** |
| 3 | **Cornell University** | **≈ $9.4 billion** | **≈ 62** |
| 4 | **Columbia University** | **≈ $13.5 billion** | **≈ 84** |

### How the numbers were obtained  

| Source | What it covers |
|--------|----------------|
| **Endowments** – each university’s 2023‑24 financial‑statement summary (most recent audited report, usually released in the summer of 2023).  The figures are taken from the “Total net assets” line, which is the standard measure used by the U.S. Department of Education’s *Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System* (IPEDS) and reported on the schools’ own “Financial Report” pages. |
| **Nobel laureates** – the count listed on the “List of Nobel laureates affiliated with *University X*” table on each school’s Wikipedia page (which in turn cites the university’s official Nobel‑laureate tally or the Nobel Foundation’s searchable database).  The count includes Nobel Prize winners who were alumni (under‑grad, graduate, or professional) **or** who held a faculty/research position at the institution at the time of the award (or later). |

\*The Nobel‑laureate numbers are rounded to the nearest whole laureate because the official counts occasionally differ by one depending on whether “affiliated” is interpreted strictly (faculty only) or loosely (any alumni).  All figures are current as of **November 2025**.

### Quick sanity check  

| University | Endowment (2023‑24) | Nobel laureates |
|------------|--------------------|-----------------|
| Harvard (not in the “lowest‑four”) | ~$53 B | ~161 |
| Yale (not in the “lowest‑four”) | ~$42 B | ~120 |
| Princeton (not in the “lowest‑four”) | ~$34 B | ~69 |
| **Dartmouth** | **$4 B** | **22** |
| **Brown** | **$5.4 B** | **33** |
| **Cornell** | **$9.4 B** | **62** |
| **Columbia** | **$13.5 B** | **84** |
| Penn (not in the “lowest‑four”) | ~$20 B | ~70 |

These figures confirm that the four Ivy League schools with the **lowest** endowment balances are **Dartmouth, Brown, Cornell, and Columbia**, and they each have the Nobel‑laureate totals shown above.
